clue.text: Tree in middle is removed

indicators.note: the central letter of the seven-letter synonym for 'in' is taken away

parts.note: something in, or in fashion, is popular

explanation.surface: A puzzling statement about a tree with something taken out of its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle is removed' takes out U, the fourth of seven letters, from POPULAR. 'Tree' looks like the subject but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A poplar is a tall fast-growing tree of the willow family.

clue.text: Waiting in readiness, love? Lovely!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O
lovely means nice

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether their beloved is ready and waiting, then exclaims with delight.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something held in reserve, put aside until needed later.

clue.text: Maybe Redknapp will reject international six-footer

indicators.note: rejecting something means throwing it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: Louise Redknapp is a British pop singer and television presenter, one of several famous Redknapps

explanation.surface: A footballer named Redknapp turning down a tall international player.
explanation.walkthrough: The Redknapps include football manager Harry and his son Jamie, which sends the solver to football; the one needed is Louise, the singer. A 'six-footer' is not tall here but an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects have six legs, so a wingless parasitic insect is a creature with six feet.

clue.text: Appreciate ale drunk in spring

indicators.note: in places the scrambled letters within the other word

parts.note: a rise is the source of a stream, as a spring is

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: Enjoying a beer consumed in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season; here it is a river's source. 'drunk' scrambles the ale, and 'in' places the result within.
explanation.definitionFit: To appreciate a fact is to understand or become aware of it, a synonym.

clue.text: Reproduction requires freedom of movement and finance

parts.note: play is slack or room to move, as in a rope with some play
to back a project is to finance it

explanation.surface: A statement about economic policy: free movement needs funding.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing back a recording reproduces sound or pictures previously captured.

clue.text: Childish and innocent, I'll say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken and the result is what they sound like

parts.note: innocent means pure, followed by the contraction I'll

explanation.surface: Someone owning up that they will describe themselves as childish and innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'pure I'll' runs together into the four-syllable word for juvenile.
explanation.definitionFit: Puerile behaviour is silly and immature, like that of a child; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: A male protecting friend in Gestapo?

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding something to shield it, so the outer letters go around

parts.note: a crony is a close friend or pal

explanation.surface: A man shielding a friend who is in the Nazi secret police.
explanation.walkthrough: GESTAPO is short for Geheime Staatspolizei, a word built from parts of its full name; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestapo is an example: a word formed from the initial letters or syllables of a longer name.

clue.text: Cabaret singer to return in May, perhaps, getting minimal coverage

indicators.note: in places one part inside the other

parts.note: Brian May, guitarist of Queen, is an example of a May

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the name is written backwards

parts.note: Liza Minnelli starred as the singer Sally Bowles in the film Cabaret

explanation.surface: A cabaret star making a comeback in the spring, with the press barely noticing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the month but is Brian May, guitarist of the band Queen. 'to return' reverses the singer's name, and 'in' puts it inside his.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian is a bikini wax that removes almost all pubic hair, leaving very little covered.

clue.text: Customers tell niece to dance

indicators.note: dancing letters jump about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Shoppers urging a young relative to get up and dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The patrons of a shop or business, taken collectively, are its regular buyers.

clue.text: Act to provoke first time out

indicators.note: first picks the earlier of the two places where that letter appears in the word
out means taken away, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: to stimulate is to provoke or arouse

explanation.surface: An instruction to stir something up the very first time, or a stage direction.
explanation.walkthrough: STIMULATE has two Ts; 'first time out' removes the earlier one.
explanation.definitionFit: To act a feeling is to pretend or feign it, a synonym of faking.

clue.text: Member of staff that is touring: essential part of operation?

definitions.text: Member of staff that is touring: essential part of operation?

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the outer letters go round the inner

parts.note: a staff is a rod or stick

indicators.note: the essential part of a word is its centre letter

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A description of a travelling crew member who keeps a show running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts the central letter of 'operation' inside the other pieces. The whole clue also describes the answer, a crew member on tour vital to the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadie is a crew member who travels with a band, setting up and maintaining equipment on tour.

clue.text: Box of novelties I supply

indicators.note: read as 'supple-y', in a supple, flexible way, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A trader offering a box of trinkets for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb, provide, but is read as an adverb from supple, bending the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Box is an informal British name for the TV set, as in 'what's on the box'.

clue.text: Charged entities in bulbs not functioning

indicators.note: not tells us that letters are absent from the word

parts.note: onions grow as bulbs
a machine that is functioning is on

explanation.surface: Physics of a dead light bulb: what charged particles are inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bulbs' suggests light bulbs, but the bulbs are vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Atoms or molecules carrying an electric charge, having gained or lost electrons.

clue.text: Happen to restrain attendant, resulting in injury

indicators.note: restraining holds something in, so one part encloses the other

parts.note: to be is to happen or take place, as in 'so be it'
a lackey is a servant or attendant

explanation.surface: A bystander grabs a servant, and someone ends up hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruise round the eye from a punch is a common facial injury.

clue.text: Needs tool to break rock

indicators.note: breaking smashes the letters so they reassemble differently

explanation.surface: Practical advice: you need a hammer or chisel to split rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetic piece of the mineral magnetite, a naturally occurring stone.

clue.text: Help Alice, say, at opening of event

parts.note: Alice Cooper is the American shock-rock singer

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A woman named Alice lends a hand at the start of a function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alice' suggests a girl's name; here it is the rock star Alice Cooper.
explanation.definitionFit: To help is to work together with others towards a shared aim.

clue.text: One bowled over?

parts.note: in cricket an over of six balls bowled with no runs scored has a special name; and a young woman can be bowled over, swept off her feet

explanation.walkthrough: Read as cricket, it is an over bowled without conceding a run; read romantically, a young woman who has been swept off her feet.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an over from which no runs come is a maiden over; a maiden is also a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Expert paid arsonist from time to time

indicators.note: now and then, so only every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A skilled professional fire-raiser hired for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and dexterous, a synonym for expert used as an adjective.

clue.text: Audience switches off when soprano absent

indicators.note: absent means missing, so that letter is left out

parts.note: turns out means switches off, as with the lights
S is the abbreviation for soprano in music

explanation.surface: Theatre staff killing the lights when the lead singer fails to appear.
explanation.definitionFit: The number of people who come to an event, its attendance or crowd.

clue.text: Author starts to smile at last

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: to last is to linger or endure

explanation.surface: A writer finally begins to smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like 'finally' but is a verb, linger.
explanation.definitionFit: J D Salinger was the American novelist who wrote The Catcher in the Rye.

clue.text: Set out to fight with Dutch flight attendant

indicators.note: out signals letters put out of their usual order

parts.note: a war is a large-scale fight

explanation.surface: An airline crew member setting off to brawl with a Dutch passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns SET into STE.
explanation.definitionFit: On an aircraft, a member of cabin crew who looks after passengers has traditionally been called this.

clue.text: Rest of story miserable

parts.note: a story is a fib, an untruth
down means miserable or low in spirits

explanation.surface: The remainder of a gloomy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' looks like a noun, the remainder, but is the verb to take a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline on a bed or sofa for a while is to take a break and relax.

clue.text: Muck possibly misleads nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold closely, so the word holds the answer inside it

explanation.surface: Dirt may lead astray those who care for patients.
explanation.walkthrough: Muck is a small island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides, not dirt; 'nurses' are not carers but a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Muck is one of the Small Isles off the west coast of Scotland, so it is an island.

clue.text: What Trump seeks is statue of Confederalist General, according to Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: Robert E Lee led the Confederate armies in the American Civil War
a statue is an erection, something put up

explanation.surface: Linking a US president's ambition to the row over Confederate statues.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the L of 'Lee' with the R sound of 'erection': 'Lee erection' becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In 2019 Donald Trump was campaigning for a second term in the 2020 presidential vote.

clue.text: When to feed young child brown bread

indicators.note: feeding puts something into another, so one part goes inside

parts.note: a tot is a small child
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Advice on when to give a toddler wholemeal bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brown bread' looks like a type of loaf but means bread browned under a grill. It is also rhyming slang for dead, as is the answer in slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread that has been browned by heat under a grill or in a toaster.

clue.text: Source of oil I have seen around southernmost part of Portugal

definitions.text: Source of oil I have seen around southernmost part of Portugal

indicators.note: around means the other letters go round this one
the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

indicators.note: in a down clue the southernmost letter is the last one written

explanation.surface: A traveller noting the oil-bearing trees seen across the Algarve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts L, the last letter of Portugal, between O and IVE. The whole clue also describes the answer: olive trees grow across the Algarve, Portugal's southern region.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive oil is pressed from the fruit of the olive tree, so the fruit is a source of oil.

clue.text: Film dog eating master's fruit

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one part encloses the other

parts.note: Toto is Dorothy's dog in the film The Wizard of Oz
MA is a master's degree, Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A cinema dog stealing its owner's fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a tomato is the fruit of the plant, though usually cooked as a vegetable.

clue.text: A nameless sentimental person is fragrant

indicators.note: nameless means without the letter N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: a romantic is a sentimental, idealistic person

explanation.surface: An anonymous soppy person smells nice.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromatic means having a pleasant, distinctive smell, a synonym for sweet-smelling.

clue.text: Exploit tax cuts, becoming loathed

indicators.note: cuts into, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: an exploit is a deed, a feat
to tax is to test or strain someone

explanation.surface: Tax avoidance schemes make someone hated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploit' and 'tax' look like a verb and a noun about money; they are the nouns deed and the verb test.
explanation.definitionFit: Detested means hated intensely, a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: New anaesthetic for bottom

parts.note: ether was an early general anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A fresh numbing agent for a sore behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' is an adjective here, lower, as in the nether regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or under, as the lowest part of something.
